questions.stem: What happens to a shape when it is enlarged by a negative scale factor?

options.text: It appears on the opposite side of the centre and is inverted
It gets smaller and stays on the same side of the centre
It gets bigger and stays on the same side of the centre

questions.explanation: A negative scale factor causes the image to appear on the opposite side of the centre of enlargement, and the image is inverted (upside down).

questions.stem: A shape is enlarged by scale factor $-2$ from the origin. Point $P(3, 1)$ maps to:
questions.explanation: Multiply each coordinate by the scale factor: $3 \times (-2) = -6$ and $1 \times (-2) = -2$, giving $(-6, -2)$.

questions.stem: An enlargement has scale factor $-\frac{1}{3}$. How does the image compare to the original?

options.text: Smaller and on the same side of the centre
Larger and on the opposite side of the centre
Larger and on the same side of the centre
Smaller and on the opposite side of the centre, inverted

questions.explanation: The magnitude $\frac{1}{3}$ is less than 1, making the image smaller. The negative sign means the image is on the opposite side of the centre and inverted.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of length 12 cm, 8 cm, and 10 cm. It is enlarged by scale factor $\frac{1}{4}$. What are the side lengths of the image?
A shape has area $36 \text{ cm}^2$ and is enlarged by scale factor $-3$. What is the area of the image?
questions.explanation: Area is multiplied by the square of the scale factor: $36 \times (-3)^2 = 36 \times 9 = 324 \text{ cm}^2$. Area is always positive.

questions.stem: Which scale factor produces an image that is larger than the original and on the opposite side of the centre?
questions.explanation: A scale factor of $-2$ has magnitude greater than 1 (making it larger) and is negative (placing it on the opposite side of the centre).

questions.stem: In an enlargement with scale factor $-1$, the image is equivalent to which other transformation?

options.text: No transformation (the shape stays the same)
A $180°$ rotation about the centre of enlargement

questions.explanation: An enlargement with scale factor $-1$ maps every point to the opposite side of the centre at the same distance, which is identical to a $180°$ rotation about that point.
